The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting is based on PISA’s technical standards for representative inference to the population of 15-year-olds in participating countries. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the specific weighting implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. Analysts using the OECD PISA database should apply the provided sampling weights and follow the PISA Reader’s Guide for variance estimation; this factsheet itself does not describe any custom reweighting or unweighted estimation.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 country factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in the Dominican Republic performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to 2015 and 2018. It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 baseline and Level 5/6 top performers), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles) and gender. The assessment uses two two-hour tests with different subject combinations across students, plus student and school questionnaires; the factsheet notes that creative thinking and financial literacy were included as additional/optional components but are not covered in this note. The factsheet also flags that PISA 2022 was delayed to 2022 due to COVID-19 and that caution is required only for countries not meeting sampling standards; the Dominican Republic met quality standards. No student-level ML modeling is conducted in this document; it is descriptive reporting based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database.
